two kinds of work # the app has one engine and two completion rules. keeping them apart is the central design decision, so it is worth stating plainly before anything else. chat verified tasks best for thinking out loud, exploring a folder, drafting a report work that must be machine-certified completion rule the model stops; a person reads the answer frozen acceptance checks decide, and a person approves each step evidence tool output is shown in the transcript provenance-bound checks over real file digests, recorded in a sqlite journal can a chat message count as proof? not applicable never writes exact diff plus allow once per-step approval, then execution and verification model freedom a bounded loop with a todo list a frozen, approved plan with retry budgets a chat message, a tool result, or an approval can never satisfy a mission check. a verified run never writes through the chat

the four local roles # each role is a separate gguf model served by a local llama-server bound to 127.0.0.1 . the harness picks roles per turn; you can see the state of all four in the models menu. role model what it does port act lfm3-1.7b plans, calls tools, reads output, writes the deliverable 8080 look lfm3-vl-2b observes one image at a time and reports what it sees 8081 hear and speak lfm3-audio-2b transcribes recordings verbatim, and speaks answers through llama-tts 8082 decide d1-2b routes each turn and answers the two decision gates 8083 only the acting model is agentic. the other three have narrow, typed jobs, and the harness will not hand any of them the planning loop. the models page explains each role, its measured strengths, and its documented limits.

what it will not do # the constraints below are enforced in code, not just documented: no file write or edit from chat without an explicit per-action approval. no path outside the workspace folder, whether reached directly, through .. , or through a link. no shell tool in chat. there is no command execution surface in the interface. no remote speech recognition, audio upload, or cloud transcription. no background model downloads. only the models menu, only after a click. no browsing, cloud fallback, or hidden network calls at runtime. no pass without provenance-bound evidence, and no weakening of a check during retry. no concurrent workspace-mutating runs, and no silent resume after an interruption. no owned model or tool process left running after the app exits. the privacy, security, and licensing page lists the three network paths that do exist and the exact scope of each.

before you begin # disk. about 5 gb for all four model roles. the first two roles below need roughly 2.2 gb. memory. 8 gb of ram is the practical minimum for chat with the text model. more helps when vision, voice, and routing run at the same time. a folder to work in. not your whole drive and not a system folder. a project folder, a notes folder, or a copy of one is ideal — the folder chip is a hard boundary for every tool. no gpu, no account, no key. the bundled runtime is cpu-only. nothing asks you to sign in.

5. approve the diff # read the card the way you would read a patch. it shows the full path inside your folder and the exact bytes that will be written. allow once executes that one action and nothing else. the next write needs its own approval. deny leaves the file untouched and tells the model not to retry the same change. pending cards expire after ten minutes, and decisions are stored with the transcript so a restart does not resurrect a stale approval. more detail, including what the harness refuses before you ever see a card, is in approvals and safety .

chat is the main surface. one bounded turn at a time, a visible route, tools confined to one folder, and a person who approves every write.

anatomy of a turn # a turn starts when you send a message and ends when the model stops, hits a limit, or you press stop . each turn can use at most twelve tool rounds. route. if the decision model is installed and your message is at least 24 characters, d1 classifies it into a task shape before the acting model runs. the chosen intent, its source, the confidence, and the local roles for the turn appear in the transcript and are carried into the system prompt. act. the acting model streams its reply and can call tools. reads and searches execute immediately; writes and edits become pending actions. gate. before a write action becomes an approval card, the write gate compares it with your latest request. after the first batch of read-only results, the evidence gate judges whether those observations are sufficient. approve. a pending write appears inline with its path and exact content or

routing # the decision model is a classifier, not an agent. it answers with a label from a closed set and a confidence in basis points; the harness owns the floor. intent meaning general ordinary conversation; no specialist role needed explore map a folder or find files summarize read sources and condense them related trace how files relate to one another report produce a markdown deliverable vision inspect an image voice work from a recording or transcript routing rules that matter in practice: messages shorter than 24 characters skip d1 entirely, so greetings cost nothing. a confident non-general answer (at least 55%) replaces a calibrated keyword route. a confident general answer keeps the turn conversational. if d1 is absent, unavailable, too slow, below the floor, or returns an undeclared label, the keyword route stands. routing selects capability hints only . it cannot grant a tool

decision gates # d1 is consulted at two more points inside a turn. each has its own typed contract, a closed label set, a harness-owned confidence floor, and a 12-second budget. write gate — before an approval card is created for write_file or edit_file . it asks whether the proposed change is aligned with, uncertain about, or contradicts your latest request. answer behaviour aligned the approval card is shown as usual uncertain the card is shown with an advisory note contradicts , confidence at or above 7,500 bps a hold: no card is shown, nothing is written, and the model is told not to retry the same change anything below the floor, slow, or absent the approval card is shown as usual evidence gate — after the first batch of read-only tool results. it asks whether those observations are sufficient, insufficient, or off-topic for the request, with a floor of 6,500 bps. anything other tha

tools in a turn # the acting model is offered a fixed set: list_files , read_file , search_files , related_files , write_file , and edit_file . two more are granted only when their model is provisioned: look for the vision model, transcribe for the audio model. the tool reference documents each one. the runtime accepts native streamed tool calls and a fenced ` tool json block for models that cannot emit a native call. both paths go through the same approval gate, so the fallback cannot bypass consent.

context window # the acting model is served with a 32,000-token window. each request carries a fixed system prompt, the newest 240 messages capped at about 96,000 characters (roughly 24,000 tokens, leaving room for tool output and the reply), temperature 0.3, and at most 1,024 output tokens. older messages fall out of the request window before they fall out of the transcript. the transcript is complete; the context is bounded. long sessions therefore keep their history on disk and a recent slice in the prompt.

image attachments # +img in the composer accepts a png, jpeg, webp, or gif up to 20 mb. the file is copied to .attachments/<uuid>-<name>.<ext> inside the workspace and a workspace-relative instruction is inserted into the message. the model inspects it with look , which loads the image through the local vision model. an attachment is user-initiated, stays inside the workspace, and is never a model write. delete the .attachments folder whenever you like; the transcript keeps the reference, and the image is simply gone. the vision model observes one image at a time and receives measured facts — format, byte length, and pixel dimensions — because it cannot know them by itself.

voice input # the microphone button records with the browser's mediarecorder , decodes and resamples the clip to 16 khz mono wav, and sends it as base64 to rust. the local audio model receives an input_audio content part and returns verbatim text, which lands in the composer for you to edit before sending. no audio leaves the machine. the transcription is not sent automatically; you review it. the audio role needs both lfm3-audio-2b-q4_k_m.gguf and its mmproj . without them the microphone path reports that the voice model is unavailable. the operating system may ask for microphone permission on first use.

voice replies # speak on any answer, or the header voice replies toggle, calls synthesize_speech , which renders one answer with llama-tts using the same lfm3-audio-2b weight and mmproj that listen. the pinned runtime is b11960. the harness uses the documented --tts-voice female|male option and the model card's audio sampling defaults. a 120-second watchdog kills the owned llama-tts process if it hangs. the temporary wav is removed after it is returned. if the voice pair is incomplete, windows falls back to the offline system voice and labels it system-sapi , so you can tell which voice spoke. linux has no system-voice fallback and reports the local voice as unavailable. the health report exposes voice_output.backend = "lfm3-tts" , model = "lfm3-audio-2b" , and lfm3_tts_weights when the binary and both files are present.

sessions # conversations are stored in chat.db in the trusted data directory, with rename, delete, and new-chat controls in the sidebar. pending approvals are persisted with the transcript, so a restart does not silently drop or silently apply one. a turn that the app stopped in the middle of comes back marked cancelled rather than being replayed. nothing resumes on its own.

what chat is not # chat output is not verified work . no chat message, tool result, or approval can satisfy a mission check, and a verified run never writes through the chat approval path. if a result has to be machine-certified — a report with required facts, a structured extraction, a screenshot review — use verified tasks , which freezes the acceptance contract before execution and records provenance for every check. development demo mode ?demo=1 in a development build renders the verified-task surface only. chat is intentionally unavailable there and says so. the production bundle contains no demo bridge at all.
four small models, each with one job. they are never downloaded in the background, never fetched from a url you did not approve, and never leave your machine.

the four roles # role model job context port act lfm3-1.7b planning, bounded acting, and short synthesis 32,000 tokens 8080 look lfm3-vl-2b bounded visual observation of one image at a time per-image 8081 hear and speak lfm3-audio-2b verbatim transcription; speech output through llama-tts per-clip 8082 decide d1-2b route classification and the two decision gates closed labels 8083 only lfm3-1.7b is agentic. the harness records each profile's measured strengths and documented weaknesses in agent::profile , and uses those limits — not a generic default — to cap turns, tool calls, replanning, and plan size.

lfm3-1.7b — the acting model # good at short instruction following, strict tool envelopes, concrete local edits, and using concrete failure feedback. bad at long-horizon planning without a written plan, recalling content it has not read, self-certification, inventing figures, and recovering from repeated failures. those limits become harness rules: a job must write a todo list before acting, unread sources are named in the prompt, a repeated identical call is refused, and finish requires the output to exist on disk. sampling follows the model card: temperature 0.1, top-k 50, repetition penalty 1.1.

lfm3-vl-2b — the vision model # observes one image at a time and reports what it sees. because it cannot know technical facts about a file by looking, the harness supplies measured format, byte length, and pixel dimensions alongside the image. it never runs the planning loop.

lfm3-audio-2b — hearing and speaking # transcribes verbatim. it is not an analyst: it does not label speakers, add timestamps, or summarise. recordings arrive with measured container facts (duration, sample rate, channels) from the harness. the same weight, through llama-tts , renders spoken replies.

d1-2b — the decision model # answers over a closed label set: a task shape for routing, and aligned/uncertain/contradicts or sufficient/insufficient/off-topic for the gates. its confidence must clear a harness-owned floor or the deterministic keyword route wins. it is not agentic and cannot call tools.

performance and hardware # the bundled runtime is cpu-only and starts servers with -ngl 0 . no gpu backend ships in any installer; the 594 mb cuda backend is excluded deliberately, so no nvidia code is redistributed. text inference is the practical bottleneck. a measured desk_task acceptance run completed in 5.99 s wall time including model startup, with a 1,603,924 kb (about 1.53 gib) peak llama-server memory on the release machine. running all four roles at once costs memory, not correctness. 8 gb is a workable minimum for chat alone; more headroom makes vision, voice, and routing comfortable alongside it. expect cpu inference to be slower than a gpu build. the project publishes measured numbers rather than speed claims; the multi-model benchmark records them with caveats.

endpoints and external servers # each role has a loopback default: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 for text, :8081 for vision, :8082 for audio, and :8083 for d1. you can point a role at another endpoint with lfm3_text_url , lfm3_vision_url , lfm3_audio_url , or lfm3_d1_url , and rename the served identity with the matching *_model variable. --external ( lfm3_reuse_external_servers ) tells the cli to reuse an already-running loopback server instead of owning one. under lfm3_profile=packaged , the engine refuses to start with a non-loopback endpoint or with the download flag on. see configuration .

removing a model # delete its folder inside the models folder, then choose reload installed models . nothing else references the weights: chat history lives in chat.db , verified evidence lives in the run journal, and neither embeds model bytes. do not edit a verified file the sha-256 is the identity of the file. replacing a .part file, truncating a download, or swapping in a different quantization makes the role fail verification. download again, or supply a build that matches the pinned digest.

licensing # the weights are not shipped and not sublicensed by this project. each model keeps the terms on its own liquid ai model card, shown in the app as lfm open license (see the model card) . downloading does not relicense them. the application source is mit. the bundled llama.cpp runtime is mit, its openmp dependency is apache-2.0 with llvm exceptions, and the windows visual c++ dlls are microsoft redistributables. the full matrix is in privacy, security, and licensing .

the approval card # a pending write or edit appears inline in the conversation with: the full path inside your workspace; the exact content for a new file, or an exact diff for an edit; allow once and deny ; the time it was proposed, so the ten-minute expiry is not a surprise. what each choice does: choice effect allow once executes that single action, returns its real output to the model, and continues the turn. the next write needs its own approval. deny leaves the file untouched and tells the model not to retry the same change. approve and let it expire after ten minutes the action is no longer executable. nothing is written. stop during a turn cancels the stream and any pending approval in that turn. 1 2 3 4 5 the foot of a real approval card, with the verdicts that let it appear and the pending write beneath it. the path and diff sit above this crop. numbers match the list below · c

before a card ever appears # several refusals happen earlier, so the card you see is already the plausible subset of what the model wanted: grant check. a tool that was not offered this turn is refused before any path resolution or side effect. path confinement. every model-supplied path goes through one shared resolver, used by chat, jobs, and mission checks, so they cannot disagree about what an escape is. write gate. before the card is created, d1 compares the change with your latest request. a confident contradicts holds it: no card, no write, and the model is told not to retry. duplicate refusal. a repeated identical call is refused instead of quietly looping.

path rules in detail # the resolver accepts relative paths inside the canonical workspace root. it also accepts a path that begins with the exact trusted workspace root, because models sometimes echo it back; that prefix is stripped, and any other absolute path is still rejected. the following are refused outright: parent components ( .. ) anywhere in the path; absolute paths outside the workspace; reserved device names; any component that is a symbolic link or reparse point — this closes the "innocent folder, link to elsewhere" route; a path whose canonical form falls outside the workspace root; for reads, a path that does not exist or is not a file. writes to a path whose parent does not exist yet are built forward, so a new out/report.md lands as requested rather than in the workspace root. links are not followed if your workspace contains a junction or symlink to another drive, tools

the two gates # both gates are advisory and both are answered by the decision model when it is installed. full behaviour is on the chat page; the safety-relevant summary is: gate when can it authorize? what a confident answer does write gate before a write or edit becomes a card no holds a contradiction (at or above 7,500 bps) or adds an uncertainty note evidence gate after the first read-only results no adds a note to state what evidence is missing (anything but sufficient, at or above 6,500 bps) if d1 is absent, slow, low-confidence, or returns a label outside its contract, the gate stays silent and behaviour is exactly what it was before the gate existed. a gate can never approve, deny, execute, or weaken anything.

approvals versus verified tasks # verified tasks use a different approval surface, because they approve plans , not just diffs: the plan is frozen with its acceptance checks and approved before any step runs. each step's execution is recorded with provenance in the run journal. a retry keeps the same frozen contract; it cannot loosen a check. chat and verified work share the engine, the model manager, and the process supervisor, but not their completion rules or their approval records. see verified tasks .

interruptions # a turn stopped mid-way comes back marked cancelled, not replayed. a verified run killed mid-attempt is reported interrupted ; the next boot reconciles it and does not resume it. a job that the engine stopped in the middle of is reported interrupted rather than resumed. nothing that was pending at the moment of an interruption is applied later on the harness's own initiative.

what stays your responsibility # the harness narrows what can happen; it does not review content for you. you are still the person who decides: whether the diff is what you asked for, and whether it is correct; whether the folder you chose is the right one for this work; whether the model's claims about the files are plausible — read the cited file when it matters; whether to trust a downloaded artifact from outside the app (the pinned downloads are verified; a file you copied in is your own provenance problem); whether to install a release whose checksum does not match. the design assumption is not that the model is trustworthy. it is that the person is in the loop, and that the interesting failure modes are visible.
a job is open-ended work: no frozen step list, a live todo list the model maintains, and a required output that must exist on disk before the job can pass.

the three phases # plan. before any workspace action, the model must call todo_write with one to eight short steps. the plan cannot be empty, and finish is refused until it exists. every step that creates or changes a file should carry a deterministic check: file_exists , dir_exists , or content_matches with a non-empty needle. work. one bounded action at a time advances an open step. marking a step done is measured: the harness runs its check against the real workspace and demotes a done claim whose check fails. once every source has been read, the tool set narrows to write_file , so the only way forward is the artifact. review. writing a non-empty deliverable opens a review turn: the model re-reads the file, compares it with the goal, and either repairs it or finishes. a first finish without a re-read is refused once with a concrete instruction; the measured proof still decides the res

what the harness enforces # the model cannot grade itself. finish is accepted only when the required output exists and is non-empty. the report carries the measured bytes and digest. a bare "finished" is refused and the model is told to keep working. every turn is evidence. each tool call and its real output is recorded, and a repeated identical call is refused instead of quietly looping. a call refused before execution never counts as "seen", so a later phase can still take it. the harness steers. unread sources are named in the prompt, and the tool set narrows to write_file once they have all been read. writes are guarded. an empty or placeholder write is refused, and a source file the job is supposed to read cannot be overwritten. a job that is supposed to produce out/report.md is told to write that file, not another one. tools follow the route. search_files and related_files are alwa

limits # bound default notes whole-job deadline 30 minutes --minutes on the cli; the form takes minutes model turns 40 --max-turns ; the desktop form takes a turn cap tool calls per turn 3 --max-calls , clamped to 1–4 plan size 1–8 steps enforced by todo_write turns without a plan 3 then the loop stops as stalled turns without a write 6 then the loop stops as stalled the acting model's profile is the ceiling on all of these. a request for more turns than the profile allows is clamped to what the model can actually sustain, rather than being honoured and then failing late.

outcomes # status meaning passed the required output exists, is non-empty, and its digest was measured unverified the loop finished without a measurable artifact to certify turn_budget the turn cap was reached deadline the minute budget ran out stalled repeated turns without progress in the loop's terms interrupted the engine stopped mid-job; it is reported, never resumed a measured artifact can still pass a stalled review turn: if the file exists and verifies, the job's result is what the file says, not what the last turn claimed.

jobs on the command line # --deliverable is detected from the goal when omitted. --events - writes durable json lines to stdout. the full flag list is in the cli reference . a measured example from the project's own run log: a four-turn job — plan ( todo_write ), work ( read_file notes.md ), work ( write_file 483 bytes to out/report.md ), review ( read_file out/report.md ) — exited 0 with status: "passed" and the report carrying the measured 483 bytes and digest 35b845745a0c6a4a .

job versus task # lfm3 job and the desktop job panel lfm3 task plan written by the model in the loop frozen and validated before execution approval the same workspace tools and approval path each step approved before it runs shape model-chosen, one action at a time a fixed ordered plan, every step with a check best for discovery, extraction, open-ended drafting predictable, reviewable, repeatable work lfm3 task also enforces the plan floor: --steps caps the plan (default 16), --min-steps refuses a plan that collapses into one call (default 2), and every step must declare at least one check. a write_file or edit_file step whose checks name no file path is rejected before the acceptance is frozen, so an untestable step never runs.

where jobs live # jobs are stored in jobs.db in the trusted data directory. events arrive on the lfm3:job-event channel. a job the engine stopped in the middle of is reported as interrupted rather than resumed, matching the rule for verified runs.

h: When a job does not finish
x: when a job does not finish # most honest failures are a goal that is too broad for a 1.7b model. practical adjustments, in order: name the output path. a deliverable in the goal is frozen as the required artifact. narrow the source set. instead of "read the project", say "read notes/*.md ". give it one job. splitting "summarise, then rewrite, then chart" into three jobs beats raising the turn cap. raise the deadline only after the goal is narrow. more turns on a vague goal produce repetition, not progress.
when a result has to be machine-certified, it runs as a mission. the checks are frozen before execution, every step is approved, and a chat message can never satisfy a check.

the four shipped missions # mission inputs what it does status desk_task goal text change approved workspace files and prove every change with a check accepted end-to-end with the real model screen_qa screenshot, written spec check a screenshot against criteria and cite visible evidence human_review_only voice_intake audio, output schema turn a spoken note into schema-valid json grounded in the transcript human_review_only doc_extract document image, fields read requested fields and prove each value is grounded human_review_only only desk_task has a completed real-model acceptance record. the three semantic missions are refused by the engine with a stated reason and the ui shows the badge with start disabled. that is not a bug to work around; it is the qualification gate described below.

how a run executes # freeze. the mission manifest plus your input produce a frozen acceptance contract with a hash. nothing after this point can weaken it. plan. the planner drafts steps bounded by the mission's limits.max_steps . approve. you approve the plan before any step runs. execute and verify. each step's tool calls run and its deterministic checks are evaluated against the real workspace. evidence records the digest of the file it actually read. retry with a budget. a failed step consumes a retry under the recovery budget. a retry uses a different strategy where one exists; it never relaxes a check. report. the run ends passed only when every frozen step check and the final output contract pass. the report carries the acceptance hash, per-step attempts, check evidence, observed versus expected output digests, and the journal count. a run that cannot make progress ends incomplete

check kinds # deterministic checks are evaluated against real files and digests: check meaning file_exists the named artifact is present dir_exists the named directory is present content_matches the file contains a required term content_absent the file does not contain a forbidden term json_schema the artifact validates against a frozen schema numeric_consistency numbers in the output agree with the frozen input report_complete every required section of a report is present semantic checks consult a bounded local judge. each result carries provenance: the evidence chain ( d1 or vl->d1 ), the model identity, the exact prompt and raw response, the label, the confidence in basis points, the frozen threshold, and the output pointers that were judged. check judge question vl_criterion vision, then d1 does the image satisfy this written criterion? d1_noul d1 is this claim supported, unsupported

h: Semantic evidence cannot manufacture a pass
x: semantic evidence cannot manufacture a pass # this is the part of the harness most worth understanding, because it is where a plausible-looking system usually cheats. a mission must declare a semantic policy. packaged missions using semantic checks declare mode: human_review_only , a minimum confidence, and a reason; the engine refuses to start them. automatic passing requires a frozen holdout qualification: at least three packaged runs and zero confident false completions. no such qualification has been performed, so automatic passing is disabled everywhere. d1_grounded first requires each field value to occur literally in the frozen input bytes. a fabricated value fails before any model is consulted. an unavailable judge, an invalid protocol answer, low confidence, or an ambiguous verdict is error , which is never treated as a pass. a deterministic failure in the same step always wins.

the journal # verified runs are recorded in a sqlite journal in the trusted data directory. lfm3 status reads it directly: a run killed mid-attempt is left interrupted . the next run reconciles one run, one step, and one attempt, does not resume it, and then proceeds normally. there is no silent resume and no ghost step. lfm3 retry creates a linked run with the same frozen acceptance contract. the link is recorded, so you can follow a retry chain without trusting a log line.

fixtures and adversarial cases # the desk_task fixture set under tests/fixtures/desk_task/ covers a passing run, a recoverable first-write failure, a wrong-content run that must never pass, and adversarial fixtures for an unsatisfiable required term and an output path outside the workspace. expected facts live in tests/golden/desk_task/ . the packaged real-model acceptance records eight cases: case result success exit 0, passed , one attempt, 5.99 s failure exit 1, incomplete / no_progress , four attempts, no false pass escape exit 1 before planning, no file outside the workspace retry exit 0, passed on attempt 2 after a denied first write crash owned model killed after attempt.started ; no false pass unavailable closed loopback endpoint; exit 1, no owned server timeout one-second deadline; owned server terminated missing empty models directory; exit 1, no download, no server every case

writing a mission # a mission is one json file in the missions directory. the shipped desk_task is the shortest complete example: rules the loader enforces: tools listed in the mission are the only ones granted, and path confinement still applies. required_artifacts are the output contract. a run cannot pass without them. limits cap the plan and the retries. command_templates is empty for general work; missions that author shell commands are a separate, deliberately narrow surface. a mission that uses semantic checks must declare a semantic policy with a mode, a confidence floor, and a reason.

separation from chat # chat verified task approval unit one diff one plan, then step evidence completion the model stops frozen checks and output contract proof transcript, for a person to read journal with digests and provenance retry you send another message budgeted retry under the same contract can it pass work it did not do? n/a no: checks read the real workspace the engine is shared. the rules are not. anything that must be certified belongs here, not in a conversation.
tools are capabilities the harness grants per turn, not a plugin surface. each one is bounded by the chosen folder, and the offered list is enforceable, not advisory.

grant rules # context what is granted chat list_files , read_file , search_files , related_files , write_file , edit_file chat, vision installed adds look chat, audio installed adds transcribe job loop search_files and related_files always; look and transcribe only when the route selects their model; narrows to write_file once every source is read verified mission exactly the tools listed in its manifest, still path-confined chat has no shell tool, and no configuration adds one. general tasks cannot author a shell command either.
file tools #

list_files # maps a directory tree. arguments: an optional path (defaults to the workspace root). directory walking stops at depth 4 and at 500 entries, appending a truncation marker. target , .git , node_modules , and .svn are skipped. output is clipped at 32,000 characters.

read_file # opens one text file. arguments: path . files above 1 mib are refused with the limit in the error, rather than read partially. output is clipped at 32,000 characters. only files inside the workspace, with no link or reparse point anywhere in the path, are readable.

write_file # creates or replaces a file. arguments: path , content . requires approval in chat; a job's write guards also refuse empty or placeholder content. content is limited to 1 mib. missing parent directories are created, so out/report.md works in a fresh folder. the write is atomic, and the tool returns the byte length and digest of what it wrote.

edit_file # replaces one exact occurrence. arguments: path , old_text , new_text . old_text must be non-empty and must occur exactly once ; zero or multiple matches are errors, not guesses. new content is limited to 1 mib and the result is written atomically. requires approval in chat.
search tools #

search_files # matches names and text across the workspace without a shell. arguments: query , optional path , optional max_results (default 20, clamped to 1–40). walks at most 4,000 entries to depth 10 and skips target , .git , node_modules , .svn , dist , and .lfm3 . each file is scanned up to 512 kib; snippets are 160 characters, up to three per file. every hit reports how many matches were found and how many were shown.

related_files # compares one file's distinctive terms with the other text files. arguments: path , optional max_results (default 10, clamped to 1–30). common stop words are removed so the comparison keys on distinguishing terms. use it to answer "what else belongs with this file?" without the model guessing from filenames.
sense tools #

look # inspects one image through the local vision model. arguments: path , instruction . png, jpeg, webp, and gif are supported. the harness prepends measured facts: format, byte length, and pixel dimensions. the model observes one image at a time and never receives the planning loop. requires the vision role and its mmproj .

transcribe # returns verbatim text for one recording. arguments: path . wav, mp3, flac, ogg, and m4a are supported. the result includes measured container facts: duration, sample rate, and channel count. it does not label speakers, add timestamps, or summarise; that is deliberate, because the model is not an analyst and inventing structure is worse than omitting it. requires the audio role and its mmproj .

speak # renders one answer as speech through llama-tts . used by speak and voice replies , not offered to the acting model as a planning tool. one 120-second watchdog guards the owned process. the temporary wav is deleted after it is returned. requires the audio role and its mmproj ; windows can fall back to the offline system voice labelled system-sapi .

structural tools # these are not file tools and do not touch disk. tool used by purpose todo_write job loop writes the plan, one to eight steps, each with an optional deterministic check finish job loop ends the job. refused until the required output exists and is non-empty todo_write is the plan gate: no workspace action is accepted before a non-empty plan exists, and a step that claims done is demoted when its check fails against the real workspace. finish is the honesty gate: the report carries the measured byte length and a content digest recomputed from the file it re-read. a bare "finished" is refused.

error behaviour # tool errors are returned to the model as real output, not hidden. that is what lets a small model correct itself: error cause outsideworkspace a path with .. , an absolute path outside the root, or a canonical escape reparsepoint a symbolic link, junction, or reparse point anywhere in the path notfound / notafile / notadirectory the target does not match the requested access notgranted the tool was not offered this turn output limit the file or directory exceeds a documented cap a refused call that never executed does not count as an observation for later phases, so the model can still take the same action once the phase allows it.

one process tree, no sidecar, no loopback control server. the webview talks to an embedded engine through typed commands and listens to durable events.
the shape of it # production uses no python sidecar and no localhost engine http server. the headless cli uses the same rust harness for diagnostics and real-model acceptance.
components #

apps/ui — the interface # react 19, typescript 5.9, and vite 8. it opens on chat, shows the decision route and local model roles, accepts image attachments and voice input, reads answers aloud with the local voice, and keeps verified missions one click away. the production bundle contains no demo bridge; ?demo=1 exists only in development and renders the verified-task surface with chat unavailable.

apps/desktop — the shell # the tauri 2 shell embeds one engine and exposes typed commands and durable events to the webview. it runs the multi-model chat turn loop and the approval gates, and it owns every child process through a kill-on-close windows job object or a linux process group. key modules: file responsibility src-tauri/src/commands.rs the typed command surface the webview may call src-tauri/src/chat.rs chat turn loop, routing, gates, attachments, voice src-tauri/src/downloads.rs the pinned model catalog and verified download src-tauri/src/engine.rs embedded engine lifecycle src-tauri/src/setup.rs read-only discovery and setup.json src-tauri/src/jobs.rs job records and the job stream src-tauri/src/events.rs event delivery to the webview

crates/lfm3-harness — the engine # the engine is a plain rust library, which is why the desktop app and the cli cannot drift apart: frozen acceptance contracts and mission manifests; planning, execution, verification, and the recovery controller; confined tools and the shared path resolver; provenance-bound deterministic checks and the semantic judge contract; model leases and process supervision; the sqlite run journal and the chat transcript store.
crates/lfm3-cli — the headless binary # doctor , missions , models , plan , run , status , retry , task , and job . it links the same engine and uses the same configuration loader.

a chat turn, in order # the webview calls a typed command with the message and any attachments. the engine opens or resumes the conversation in chat.db and checks that no turn is already live. if d1 is installed and the message is long enough, the router classifies it against a closed label set. the keyword route stands if the answer is missing, slow, or below the floor. the acting model is called with a bounded context: fixed system prompt, newest 240 messages capped near 96,000 characters, temperature 0.3, at most 1,024 output tokens. tool calls are executed by the confined registry. reads run; writes become pending actions after the write gate. tool results, gate outcomes, and message deltas are emitted as durable events. the turn ends after at most twelve tool rounds, or on stop , which cancels the stream and pending approvals.

a verified run, in order # the mission manifest plus input produce a frozen acceptance contract and its hash. the planner drafts steps; the plan is approved before execution. the executor runs one step at a time, each tool call path-confined. the verifier evaluates deterministic checks against real files and records digests; semantic checks follow the mission's declared policy. failures consume the recovery budget and may replan, never relax. the coordinator writes every transition to the journal and emits events. the run ends passed only on a complete contract, otherwise incomplete with a reason.

event channels # channel carries lfm3:chat-event chat message deltas, route and gate results, approval requests and decisions, voice results lfm3:job-event job turns, phases, todo state, tool calls, status lfm3:run-event verified-run journal events: attempts, checks, retries, completion events are durable, not cosmetic: the journal and the database are the source of truth, and the ui rehydrates from them after a restart.

process supervision # model servers are child processes the harness owns, not services you manage. platform mechanism on exit windows job object with kill-on-close the entire job is terminated linux process group per child the group is terminated a platform with neither containment refuses to start children rather than leaking them. the supervisor reports which mechanism it is using. on linux, each owned llama.cpp process also gets its own directory at the front of ld_library_path , so packaged libraries win over system copies. the installed smoke acceptance proves this in the negative: an externally started llama-server survives every phase, while an owned llama-server dies with the app.

state # store contents chat.db conversations, messages, pending and decided approvals jobs.db jobs and their turns runs.db runs, steps, attempts, evidence, retry links setup.json runtime paths, models folder, default workspace workspace only approved writes, plus .attachments/ no store is shared with the model servers, and no model output is trusted as state. the engine reads the file it wrote to report a digest, rather than trusting the content it sent.

h: Why it is built this way
x: why it is built this way # embedded, not sidecar. a separate engine process would add a supervisor, an rpc surface, and a second lifecycle to get wrong. an in-process engine makes the boundary a function call. one path resolver. tools and verifiers share paths::resolve , so "inside the workspace" cannot mean two different things. typed decisions. routing and gates return declared labels with confidences, not free text. an undeclared label is a failure, not an interpretation. measured completion. every completion claim is re-derived from the filesystem. the digest in a report is recomputed from the file that was re-read. bounded everything. turns, tool calls, tool output, file sizes, retries, deadlines, and plan size all have caps. the model's profile sets them.

stack # rust stable: msvc toolchain on windows, gnu on linux. tokio, serde, reqwest, rusqlite, and sha-256 for the engine. tauri 2 for the native boundary. react 19, typescript 5.9, vite 8, vitest, and playwright for the ui. external llama.cpp b11960 for inference: no rust ffi, no version drift. the inference backend is pinned deliberately. using rust does not require changing llama.cpp, and an upgrade requires a separate compatibility qualification across all four models.
local-first is an engineering property here, not a slogan: loopback-only servers, no account, no runtime network calls, and three clearly named exceptions.

what leaves your machine # there are exactly three outbound paths, and two of them require you to act. path when what is sent model download you click download on one role an https request to huggingface.co/liquidai for a pinned file name a link you click you click it whatever that site normally receives opt-in tracing you set posthog_api_key model-call metadata; prompt and completion text only if posthog_ai_capture_content=1 the download host, file names, byte lengths, and sha-256 digests are fixed in the source. there is no "check for updates", no crash reporter, no telemetry client when the key is unset, and no remote model endpoint.

what never leaves # prompts, model replies, and tool output. the contents of any file in your workspace. images you attach, audio you record, or transcripts the audio model produces. chat transcripts, job records, and verified-run journals. your folder paths, machine name, or usage counts. speech recognition and speech synthesis both run on the local audio model. there is no cloud transcription path to disable, because there is none.

the network boundary, in code # every role's default endpoint is 127.0.0.1 : :8080 text, :8081 vision, :8082 audio, :8083 decision. under lfm3_profile=packaged the engine refuses to start if any endpoint is not loopback, or if lfm3_allow_download is on. boot-time discovery reads paths; it never contacts the network. the installers contain no updater component. you can verify the listener side yourself while the app is running: linux windows (powershell) every row should show 127.0.0.1 or ::1 , never 0.0.0.0 .

data at rest # everything the app knows lives in the trusted data directory: item sensitivity chat.db full conversation content jobs.db job goals, turns, tool output run journal steps, evidence, digests, prompts used by the judge setup.json local absolute paths models/ public model weights the data directory is protected by your operating-system account permissions, and nothing more. there is no application-level encryption, no key management, and no password. if your threat model includes someone with your unlocked account or your disk, use full-disk encryption — that is the control that fits this design. attachments are copied into .attachments/ inside the workspace , not the data directory, so they travel with the folder you chose. delete that folder to remove them.

the trust boundary # the design assumption is that model output is untrusted. concern control model writes a file you did not want exact diff, allow once , ten-minute expiry, no blanket grant model reaches outside the folder one shared path resolver; .. , absolute escapes, and links refused model runs a command no shell tool in chat; missions cannot author shell commands model lies about finishing completion is re-derived from the filesystem; the digest is recomputed from the re-read file model contradicts your request write gate hold at a 75% floor model guesses from thin evidence evidence gate note at 65% floor chat output counted as certified work separate surfaces, separate completion rules a semantic judge invents a pass grounding checks first; human_review_only ; automatic passing disabled a crashed app leaves servers running job object or process group containment, proven by smoke

h: What is still yours to do
x: what is still yours to do # the harness narrows what can happen. it does not take responsibility for your machine or your judgement: review the diff. the approval exists because you are the reviewer. approving without reading is the one control the harness cannot enforce. choose the folder deliberately. do not point it at a directory holding secrets you would not paste into a chat window. keep the operating system trusted. an attacker with your account can read the data directory and the workspace. check downloads you did not make in the app. a gguf you copied in has your provenance, not the catalog's. treat model claims as claims. a 1.7b model can be wrong confidently. open the cited file when it matters. encrypt the disk if the machine can be stolen.

reporting a problem # security issues belong in the repository's issue tracker unless they involve an undisclosed vulnerability, in which case contact the maintainer privately before publishing details. include the version, platform, and the smallest reproduction you can build; a report that names a file path and an expected versus observed result is worth ten that describe a feeling.
most problems are a missing model, a busy port, or a platform library. start with the symptom table, then run the diagnostics command it points to.

first: read the health report # on windows, run it from the install folder or through a source checkout with cargo run -p lfm3-cli -- doctor --probe-models . it reports the resolved runtime path, every model endpoint and the identity it serves, the models folder, the workspace, and every missing item.

models and downloads # a download fails or never finishes. only one role downloads at a time. cancel the active one before starting another. a failed verification discards the .part file; retry the download rather than reusing it. check free disk space — all four roles need about 4.9 gb. the sha-256 check fails. the file arrived corrupt or was modified in transit. delete the .part file and download again. do not rename a partial file into place: the digest is the identity of the weight. you copied weights in by hand. keep the repository subfolder layout, then choose reload installed models . the app verifies byte length and sha-256; a mismatched file is reported rather than used. the models folder is on another drive. set lfm3_models_dir to that folder, or set models_dir in setup.json . use an absolute path; a relative path is not resolved against your shell's working directory.

ports # the four roles use 8080, 8081, 8082, and 8083 on loopback. if another tool holds one, the role cannot start. linux windows (powershell) either stop the other process, or point the role at another loopback port with lfm3_text_url (and the matching *_url variable). if you already run your own llama-server, --external lets the cli reuse it instead of owning one.
platform issues #

windows # smartscreen. the installers are unsigned. verify the checksum from the install page, then choose more info → run anyway . there is no certificate to look for and no way to make the dialog disappear without signing the build. installed to a path with a space. that is by design ( %localappdata%\lfm3 workspace ) and exercised by the project's own smoke test. missing vc++ dlls. the bundle includes vcruntime140.dll , vcruntime140_1.dll , and msvcp140.dll . if a repair removed them, reinstall.

linux # webkitgtk errors on launch. install the development and runtime packages for webkitgtk 4.1 and gtk 3; run.sh deps prints the exact command for your distribution. appimage will not start. if fuse is missing, extract and run: a system libllama conflicts. packaged libraries are already first in ld_library_path for owned processes. if you run your own server, keep its libraries and the bundled ones on separate paths. no system voice. linux has no sapi equivalent, so an incomplete voice pair means speech output is reported unavailable rather than silently substituting a different voice.

voice # problem check microphone button does nothing os microphone permission for the app "voice model unavailable" audio gguf and its mmproj are both installed transcript is empty the clip was silent; the harness refuses an empty recording rather than inventing text speech output uses a robotic voice on windows that is the offline system voice, labelled system-sapi ; install the voice pair for the local model speech output fails on linux llama-tts is missing or the voice pair is incomplete the local audio model transcribes verbatim. it does not label speakers or add timestamps, so a transcript without them is correct behaviour, not a bug.

h: Chat behaviour that looks like a bug
x: chat behaviour that looks like a bug # a second message is refused while a turn is live. one bounded turn at a time is deliberate; the error is visible rather than queued. the turn stops by itself. a turn allows at most twelve tool rounds. ask for the next step. a write is missing its approval card. the write gate may have held it. the gate chip under the conversation states the outcome; a hold means nothing was written and the model was told not to retry. the model says it finished but the file is empty. chat is not verified work. for a measured result, use jobs or verified tasks . routing picked the wrong intent. it selects capability hints only. rephrase with an explicit verb and file name; a missing or low-confidence decision model falls back to keywords.

jobs and verified runs # status what to change turn_budget narrow the goal or produce the output sooner; raising the cap on a vague goal usually repeats work deadline same, plus a realistic minute budget stalled the loop saw three turns without a plan or six without a write; restate the goal with one concrete deliverable unverified no measurable artifact; name the required output path interrupted the engine stopped mid-run. it is never resumed; start a new job incomplete / no_progress a verified run exhausted its retries without passing. read the check evidence in the report a verified mission with human_review_only cannot be started at all. that is the qualification gate, not a configuration problem; see verified tasks .

reset state # back up first. there is no migration between versions and no recovery for a deleted transcript. what where one conversation delete it in the chat sidebar all conversations and approvals chat.db in the data directory jobs jobs.db verified-run history runs.db in the data directory workspace choice workspace in setup.json , or the folder chip models the models folder removing the whole data directory returns the app to a fresh install while keeping your workspace files untouched.

h: What to include in a bug report
x: what to include in a bug report # version from the footer or the models menu, and the platform. output of lfm3 doctor --probe-models . the model states (loaded / installed / missing) for all four roles. the exact error text, copied rather than paraphrased. the smallest workspace that reproduces it, and whether a fresh folder behaves the same. for a verified run: the run id, so the journal state can be read with lfm3 status <run-id> . reports that name the file path and say what was expected versus observed are the ones that get fixed.

this documentation # the pages under /docs are generated from docs/guide/*.md . navigation order, page titles, descriptions, and the ledes live in scripts/build-docs.mjs ; the markdown holds only content. the generator supports a deliberately small markdown subset: ## and ### headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, inline code, links, fenced code, unordered and ordered lists, tables, --- , and callouts: variants are note , tip , warn , and danger . heading ids are generated from the heading text, so cross-page links can point at page.html#section and stay stable. links ending in .md are rewritten to .html automatically. the build also writes docs/search-index.json for the in-page search and updates the generated block in sitemap.xml . nothing is fetched at runtime, and the output is plain html with one small script for search, copy buttons, and scrollspy.

adding a mission # copy a manifest in missions/ and change name , inputs , tools , checks , and output . validate it with lfm3 missions . add fixtures under tests/fixtures/<mission>/ and expected facts under tests/golden/<mission>/ . run the fixture suite, then a real-model acceptance before claiming the mission is supported.
